cards.title: Tag COGS in Shopify to Capture Discount Margin Compression
cards.summary: Without per-product COGS, percentage gross-margin assumptions miss discount-driven margin compression and corrupt every downstream metric.
cards.use_when: Setting up reporting or evaluating profitability during promotions such as Black Friday or storewide discount events.

cards.title: When Attribution Fails: Confounding Across Channels and Sales Channels
cards.summary: Attribution is correlation; with multiple ad channels and revenue channels, causality becomes confounded and experiments are required.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to rely on attribution for a store that runs multiple ad platforms and sells across .com, retail, Amazon or wholesale.

cards.title: Geo-Lift Test Design for Measuring Incremental Ad Impact
cards.summary: Build correlated treatment and control regions from matched historical series, then measure the divergence between actual and counterfactual revenue after an intervention such as doubling Meta budget.
cards.use_when: Measuring the true incremental impact of a budget increase or a new upper-funnel channel when platform attribution is untrustworthy.

cards.title: Choose the right incrementality test by revenue scale
cards.summary: Match geo-lift, in-platform lift, and causal-impact methods to your budget level instead of running one test type everywhere.
cards.use_when: Deciding how to validate whether a paid channel or campaign is actually driving incremental revenue before increasing spend.

cards.title: Audit nine common paid-media measurement mistakes
cards.summary: A checklist of recurring tracking and account-structure errors that inflate reported ROAS and misdirect budget.
cards.use_when: Reviewing a paid media account or onboarding a new agency to find where reported performance diverges from actual business results.

cards.title: Take the right measurement actions by revenue tier
cards.summary: A staged action list for cleaning up tracking and reporting at $1–5M, $5–20M and $20M+ revenue.
cards.use_when: Planning the next round of measurement and reporting improvements for a store based on its current annual revenue.

cards.title: Set up Conversions API and treat GA4 as a redundancy layer
cards.summary: Tracking hygiene: server-side events, avoiding Shopify attribution reports, and keeping GA4 as a fallback.
cards.use_when: Auditing or rebuilding the tracking stack for a store that spends on Meta and needs reliable event data for optimisation.

cards.title: Distinguish gross and net revenue to diagnose monthly swings
cards.summary: Break revenue into gross, refunds, discounts and shipping collected before concluding why net revenue moved.
cards.use_when: Reviewing month-over-month revenue changes or diagnosing why net revenue rose or fell despite stable ad spend.

cards.title: Calculate pre-marketing contribution using explicit delivery costs
cards.summary: Separate accounting gross profit from the management contribution metric used to fund ecommerce acquisition.
cards.use_when: Setting marketing budget allocation per product or category, or when a product looks profitable but the business isn't.

cards.title: Use contribution margin to back-solve a net profit target
cards.summary: Convert a net margin target into a contribution margin target using stable operating expenses.
cards.use_when: Setting monthly profitability guardrails for paid media spend and marketing decisions.

cards.title: Calculate CAC correctly and pair it with first-purchase gross profit
cards.summary: Blended CAC, defined on new customers, is meaningless without the gross profit of a first order.
cards.use_when: Setting acquisition cost targets or evaluating whether to scale paid spend on a new-customer campaign.

cards.title: Classify marketing, content and fulfilment staff costs correctly
cards.summary: Where flexing creative spend, fulfilment labour and transaction fees belong on the P&L, and why it changes gross margin.
cards.use_when: Structuring the P&L chart of accounts, or benchmarking gross margin and contribution margin against targets.

cards.title: Control operating expenses as the main profit leak
cards.summary: Why reinvestment in ecommerce should go to marketing, not headcount, software or offices.
cards.use_when: Deciding how to deploy incremental profit, or diagnosing flat dollar profit despite revenue growth.

cards.title: Replace keystone and markup pricing with waterfall pricing
cards.summary: Price from a required contribution or net profit target upward instead of applying arbitrary multiples to product cost.
cards.use_when: Setting or repricing a product, or deciding whether a product is viable to sell at all.

cards.title: Troubleshoot the P&L from the bottom up
cards.summary: Convert P&L percentages into a diagnosis rule: a missed line means the problem lies in everything above it.
cards.use_when: Monthly P&L review to decide where to intervene in pricing, marketing spend or cost of delivery.

cards.title: Waterfall pricing from bottom to top
cards.summary: Price by working from a contribution margin target through CAC, returns, fulfillment and COGS up to a price — then test it against competitors and cut the SKU if it fails.
cards.use_when: Product selection or pricing: deciding whether to launch or keep a SKU, or setting its retail price before comparing to competitors.

cards.title: Calculate break-even ROAS and break-even CAC before any discount
cards.summary: Calculate first-order pre-ad contribution, then derive a break-even acquisition ceiling with a consistent revenue basis.
cards.use_when: Pricing, promotions and paid media planning: deciding whether a campaign, ad set or promotion is actually profitable.

cards.title: Recalculate contribution and break-even acquisition cost before discounting
cards.summary: Model discounted net revenue against all variable order costs before setting acquisition targets.
cards.use_when: Promotions and offer design: pressure-testing a discount before running it publicly or on paid acquisition.

cards.title: Use bundles to give value without eroding gross margin percentage
cards.summary: Bundling raises AOV and typically inflates shipping/fulfillment by far less than the unit count, so you can pass value to the customer while keeping margin percentage intact.
cards.use_when: Offer design and merchandising: when you want a customer-facing deal that does not destroy the unit economics the way a flat discount does.

cards.title: Design gift-with-purchase offers around the gift's true cost
cards.summary: A low-cost gift with a high perceived retail value can double AOV while giving up only a few dollars of margin.
cards.use_when: Offer design and PDP merchandising: creating a purchase incentive that lifts AOV without compressing gross margin percentage.

cards.title: Restrict flat discounting to non-moving inventory to convert stock to cash
cards.summary: Straight discounts compress margin badly, so reserve them for slow-moving stock where the alternative is not selling at all.
cards.use_when: Pricing and merchandising: clearing aged inventory or funding a cash conversion push.

cards.title: Compare contribution margin per product, not just CPA
cards.summary: Two SKUs can have very different contribution margins per sale even when a lower-priced one shows the cheaper CPA, which distorts platform bidding.
cards.use_when: Product selection and paid media structure: deciding which SKUs deserve budget and how to segment campaigns.

cards.title: Measure on a pyramid: platform metrics, finance-grade KPIs, incrementality
cards.summary: Reliability of measurement increases as you move from platform-attributed metrics up to finance-grade KPIs and incrementality tests, while speed of feedback decreases.
cards.use_when: Measurement and reporting: choosing which numbers to trust for budget decisions and how to present them to founders or a leadership team.

cards.title: Use new-customer MER instead of blended MER
cards.summary: Blended MER lets marketing take credit for returning-customer revenue that would have come back anyway, so delineate new-customer revenue over ad spend.
cards.use_when: Measurement and acquisition budgeting: indexing paid media performance over time and setting acquisition targets.

cards.title: Track LTGP to CAC on fixed time windows, not lifetime-forever
cards.summary: Divide gross profit from a customer over a defined window by the cost to acquire them, and interpret the ratio against staged bands rather than treating any result as good.
cards.use_when: Retention and acquisition planning: judging whether paid acquisition is reasonably efficient and how aggressively you can scale spend.

cards.title: Analyze new-customer versus returning-customer profit contribution separately
cards.summary: Most ecommerce profit often comes from returning customers because they cost little to re-acquire, while new customer revenue carries the ad spend.
cards.use_when: Retention planning and acquisition budgeting: deciding how hard to push new customer acquisition and how much to invest in retention channels.

cards.title: Configure Meta reporting to reduce over-attribution
cards.summary: Exclude view-through conversions and existing customers from reporting to get numbers closer to finance-grade acquisition metrics.
cards.use_when: Paid media measurement and budget decisions: auditing Meta reporting settings and frequency before scaling spend.

cards.title: Budgetting existing-customer ad spend from audience size and frequency
cards.summary: Calculate existing-customer ad spend from how many customers you have, your desired frequency, and CPM — not as a percentage of budget.
cards.use_when: Retention advertising and budget allocation: deciding how much to spend retargeting existing customers.

cards.title: Solve for the next best dollar across channels
cards.summary: Identify where the next increment of budget produces the most incremental profit by comparing marginal returns across channels, including by pulling budget out of one channel.
cards.use_when: Budget allocation and scaling decisions: deciding where to add or remove the next $10,000 of media spend.

cards.title: Read ROAS as correlation, not causation
cards.summary: ROAS relies on attribution, which links correlated events rather than proving the ad caused the purchase, so it over-credits bottom-funnel channels.
cards.use_when: Measurement, channel review and executive reporting: defending or cutting a channel when ROAS numbers look weak.

cards.title: Design geographic holdout incrementality tests for media decisions
cards.summary: Split geographies into control and treatment, change spend in one group, and measure the difference in new customer revenue to estimate true incremental impact.
cards.use_when: Measurement: validating whether a channel, campaign or budget change actually drives incremental revenue, especially for larger businesses.

cards.title: Account for cash conversion cycle before promising rapid scaling
cards.summary: The binding constraint on ecommerce growth is often the cash conversion cycle — DIIO plus DSO minus DPO — not ad efficiency or media budget.
cards.use_when: Growth planning and replenishment: setting realistic scale targets and coordinating marketing spend with inventory cash requirements.

cards.title: Read the balance sheet alongside the P&L to see real ecommerce profit
cards.summary: Reconcile profit to cash using changes in inventory, other working capital and financing rather than subtracting an ending stock balance.
cards.use_when: Founder-level reporting and growth decisions: interpreting profit figures and communicating the true cash position.

cards.title: Grade inventory and rationalize SKUs to avoid the inventory death spiral
cards.summary: Product launches that fail land as slow-moving stock, adding cash to the balance sheet and constraining growth unless you rationalize SKU count and proactively clear graded stock.
cards.use_when: Product selection, inventory management and merchandise planning: deciding which SKUs to keep, launch or clear, and how to brief the paid media team.

cards.title: Model the cash cost of scaling inventory before committing to a growth rate
cards.summary: Tripling DTC revenue requires cash for inventory far faster than most brands can fund it, and aggressive spend cuts margin via interest and poor efficiency.
cards.use_when: Setting a growth target or reorder cadence for a scaling store, or deciding whether to spend more to clear aged stock.

cards.title: Forecast new and returning customer revenue separately
cards.summary: New-customer revenue is driven by acquisition inputs while returning revenue comes from cohorts, launches and events, so they must be forecast with separate models.
cards.use_when: Building a monthly revenue forecast or media budget for an ecommerce brand.

cards.title: Derive ad spend and efficiency from regression on daily data, excluding outliers
cards.summary: Plot daily acquisition ME against spend, fit a regression after removing sale periods and sub-threshold days, and read off expected efficiency at any spend level.
cards.use_when: Setting a media budget for the coming month or checking whether a new-customer revenue goal is achievable at target efficiency.

cards.title: Do not allocate budget by in-platform ROAS across funnel positions
cards.summary: Bottom-of-funnel campaigns always show better ROAS, so reading platform ROAS alone systematically over-allocates to retargeting and branded terms.
cards.use_when: Deciding where to shift budget across Meta, Google and other campaigns in a store's media plan.

cards.title: Budget for brand even where it shows no direct ROI
cards.summary: Above roughly $30-40k/day in spend, performance marketing alone hits diminishing returns; brand associations outside the ad account improve how the ad account itself performs.
cards.use_when: Allocating marketing budget between performance channels and brand-building activity such as events, influencers and sponsorship.

cards.title: Treat the offer, not the ad account, as the primary lever
cards.summary: Budget and account structure sit at the base of the hierarchy; creative, offer, brand and product are the bigger but harder levers that actually move performance.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing flat performance and deciding whether to rebuild creative, offer or account structure rather than simply raising budget.

cards.title: Define an offer as five mechanics, not just a discount
cards.summary: An offer comprises product positioning, price architecture, value mechanic, risk reversal and urgency, of which discounting is only one option.
cards.use_when: Designing an evergreen acquisition offer or promo for a store's PDP, landing page or paid ads.

cards.title: Model discount economics through the full waterfall before running a sale
cards.summary: A 25% discount lifted AOV via higher UPT but compressed gross margin and required roughly 9x ROAS to hold the same contribution profit versus 6x at full price.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to run a flat percentage-off promotion or how deep to discount in a store.

cards.title: Find the discount depth that maximises contribution profit
cards.summary: Small discounts often reduce contribution profit because they don't lift units per transaction, and very deep discounts destroy margin faster than volume can compensate, so an optimum exists.
cards.use_when: Choosing the headline discount percentage for a promo or evergreen offer.

cards.title: Build an evergreen acquisition offer with layering that improves efficiency
cards.summary: A layered subscription offer (90-day supply, app access, mystery gift, lifetime discount) can cut the required ROAS from 6x to under 3x while raising contribution profit.
cards.use_when: Designing an evergreen acquisition offer for a consumable product where a flat discount would be too expensive.

cards.title: Use product repositioning to unlock persona-specific offers at no COGS cost
cards.summary: Keeping one SKU but repositioning it into multiple personas lets you create sharper, more congruent offers with essentially zero margin impact.
cards.use_when: Building landing pages, prospect audiences or offer variants for a hero product such as a supplement or consumable.

cards.title: Use bundles to raise units per transaction and capture fulfilment scale
cards.summary: Bundles raise UPT and improve cost-of-delivery through shipping efficiencies, but they're a relatively simple, easy offer compared with other mechanics.
cards.use_when: Designing a bundle offer for a multi-SKU store or a consumable single-SKU store.

cards.title: Track new and returning customer metrics separately in live dashboards
cards.summary: New and returning customer economics have different levers, so dashboard them separately alongside acquisition ME, profit contribution and LTV:CAC rather than relying on ROAS reports.
cards.use_when: Setting up weekly reporting or a KPI dashboard for an ecommerce brand.

cards.title: Know gross margin, product margin and contribution margin precisely
cards.summary: Before any offer or budget decision, calculate product margin versus gross margin (including variable costs) and how both flow into contribution margin.
cards.use_when: Establishing the financial baseline for pricing, offers, media spend and profitability decisions in a store.

cards.title: Let the P&L identify the constraint instead of forcing budget growth
cards.summary: Read the P&L level by level, KPI each level, and when a metric misses, trace upward to find the actual constraint — which may be cash conversion rather than media.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to increase media spend, cut costs or fix cash/inventory when profitability or growth stalls.

cards.title: Distinguish Cross-Sells (complementary product) from Upsells (more of the same)
cards.summary: Cross-sells offer a different complementary product while upsells sell a larger/multi-pack quantity of the item already in the cart, and each fits a different catalog.
cards.use_when: Designing the in-cart, checkout or post-purchase add-on step for a product page or bundle decision.

cards.title: Optimize upsells/cross-sells on incremental contribution profit, not take rate alone
cards.summary: The correct upsell is the one maximizing take rate times added AOV times gross margin, which often means a lower-take-rate, higher-margin item wins.
cards.use_when: Choosing which product to place as the in-cart or post-purchase upsell/cross-sell.

cards.title: Match add-on placement to friction level and expected take rate
cards.summary: Cart, checkout and post-purchase add-ons carry very different friction and take rates, so the offer type should change by placement.
cards.use_when: Deciding where to place an upsell or cross-sell (cart drawer, checkout, or post-purchase page).

cards.title: Anchor high then down-sell when sequencing post-purchase offers
cards.summary: Lead post-purchase with a higher-priced upsell and down-sell below it, because leading with the cheapest offer anchors prices low.
cards.use_when: Building or reordering a post-purchase upsell/down-sell sequence.

cards.title: Apply the five rules for in-cart upsells
cards.summary: Keep one offer per cart slot, prioritize relevance, high margin, simplicity and gross-margin-lift measurement.
cards.use_when: Designing the in-cart drawer upsell slot.

cards.title: Use revenue per visit (RPV) to size the post-purchase opportunity
cards.summary: RPV = post-purchase revenue ÷ post-purchase funnel visits (or average upsell value × conversion rate), with a source-cited target of 10–15%.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing whether a post-purchase upsell program is contributing enough incremental revenue.

cards.title: Structure gift-with-purchase offers that raise units per transaction without eroding margin
cards.summary: A cheap, relevant free gift can roughly double contribution margin and lower break-even ROAS, but only if the gift's perceived value is real.
cards.use_when: Building a multi-buy or bundle offer and choosing the free gift.

cards.title: Set tiered/threshold offers using the AOV distribution, not the average
cards.summary: Bimodal AOV distributions require offers targeted at each peak rather than one threshold set from the mean, which can leak margin without moving anyone.
cards.use_when: Designing threshold mechanics like free-shipping or spend-to-unlock for a catalog with varied order sizes.

cards.title: Use flat discounting rarely and only for specific scenarios
cards.summary: Straight discounting is a legitimate mechanic only for high-gross-margin SKs or grade-C inventory, and should be used one to two times a year at most.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to run a site-wide or category discount promotion.

cards.title: Segment exit-intent offers by funnel stage
cards.summary: Browse, cart and checkout exits represent different intent levels, so give generous urgency to browsers, tiny offers to cart abandoners, and risk-reversal (not discounts) to checkout abandoners.
cards.use_when: Setting up exit-intent popups or abandoned-cart/checkout email and SMS flows.

cards.title: Select and iterate the right front-end offer via four diagnostic questions
cards.summary: Choose offers by gross margin floor, AOV distribution shape, single vs multi SKU, and repeat behaviour — then test, since only about 10 of 100 possible offers are good.
cards.use_when: Choosing which front-end acquisition offer to run for a product line or campaign.

cards.title: Diagnose why front-end offers fail
cards.summary: Common failure modes: calling a bare discount an offer, miscalculating margin, using the same offer for new vs returning customers, mean-based thresholds, a wrong or uneconomic gift, an endless promo calendar, and blaming Q1 on seasonality.
cards.use_when: Reviewing a struggling or underperforming promotional calendar.

cards.title: Plan discounting by modelling AOV lift and required efficiency
cards.summary: Undisciplined discounting erodes margin unless you model AOV/UPT lift from prior discounts and the ROAS needed at the new threshold.
cards.use_when: Planning a price promotion and its paid media efficiency.

cards.title: Design bundles across SKs and as repeated same-SKU offers
cards.summary: Bundles protect contribution margin but are fundamentally an easy offer; there is more upside in creatively combining mechanics rather than stopping at a basic SK bundle.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to run a straightforward multi-buy bundle vs a layered offer.

cards.title: Consolidation beats segmentation in Meta account structure
cards.summary: Fewer campaigns and adsets generally outperform highly segmented structures, because Meta chooses where to spend based on incremental returns and cross-ad sequencing, not the siloed per-ad metrics you see.
cards.use_when: Deciding campaign/adset structure for a paid social account.

cards.title: Match Meta spend playbook and structure decisions to account size
cards.summary: The right account structure depends on spend level — the source frames three playbooks (under 50k, 50–250k, 250k+ per month) and notes media buying still matters at higher spend.
cards.use_when: Choosing how much structure and manual media buying effort to apply based on monthly ad spend.

cards.title: Use broad targeting with creative-driven audience retrieval
cards.summary: Broad targeting lets the platform's retrieval system place creative by its understanding of the ad, clustering users in high-dimensional space rather than relying on interest labels that don't capture intent.
cards.use_when: Setting targeting for a new Meta campaign or testing whether to keep interest-based audiences.

cards.title: Diagnose scaling death and ad fatigue with the cluster model
cards.summary: Ads fatigue when scaling pushes spend into colder clusters where the creative no longer convinces — the source frames this as the core limit on scaling a winning campaign.
cards.use_when: Managing a scaling campaign that is decaying or losing efficiency.

cards.title: Set cost caps and bidding at the adset level, not the ad level
cards.summary: Bidding and optimisation are inherited from the adset, so ad-level ROAS tells you what you see, not where the platform places the bid.
cards.use_when: Configuring bid strategy or cost caps in a Meta campaign and interpreting ad-level reporting.

cards.title: Diagnose whether to consolidate or segment paid campaigns
cards.summary: Five diagnostic questions about categories, margin spread, personas, regions and creative throughput determine how much ad account segmentation is commercially justified.
cards.use_when: Deciding account structure (how many campaigns/adsets and what each represents) for a store's paid social or paid search account before restructuring or scaling spend.

cards.title: Consolidation vs segmentation: the small-sample tradeoff
cards.summary: Splitting conversions across many campaigns shrinks the optimization signal each one gets, so consolidate at campaign level while allowing more freedom at adset level.
cards.use_when: Planning how many campaigns to run for a low-to-mid-spend store's paid social account.

cards.title: Set campaign structure from unit economics and AOV first
cards.summary: Different unit economics, audiences, or very high AOV with tiny conversion volume each argue against a single consolidated campaign.
cards.use_when: Choosing whether a large multi-SKU store or a high-ticket store can run a fully consolidated cold campaign.

cards.title: Drop daily bid and budget micro-tweaking; invest the time in creative
cards.summary: The source argues daily bid/budget tweaks are low-leverage compared with producing better creative and better landing pages.
cards.use_when: Deciding how an operator or media buyer should spend their weekly paid-media working hours.

cards.title: When and why to run a scaling campaign
cards.summary: A separate scaling campaign exists only to squeeze extra daily spend out of creative that has already been maxed out in its original adset.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to add a scaling campaign to a store's paid social account.

cards.title: Set adset budgets from target CPA, not the 50-conversion rule
cards.summary: Derive the total test budget from target CPA and the run duration from seasonality and time-to-purchase, instead of applying the generic 50-conversions-per-7-days guideline.
cards.use_when: Setting adset-level budgets for a small or mid-size store's cold testing structure.

cards.title: Structure cold testing around concepts, not audiences
cards.summary: Define a concept as persona × angle × offer, hold it in an adset, and rotate ad types and creative underneath it so you can read which concept earns spend.
cards.use_when: Building the creative-testing layer of a store's paid social account, or diagnosing why testing never produces a scalable winner.

cards.title: Build the sub-$50k/month 'generic' structure
cards.summary: At low spend, run a consolidation-first structure of testing, optional scaling, and optional existing-customer retargeting, with existing customers excluded from cold.
cards.use_when: Standing up a paid social account for a store spending under roughly $50k per month on ads.

cards.title: Extend from sub-$50k to $50k–$250k with commercially justified campaigns
cards.summary: At higher spend, add campaigns only where a specific commercial objective (funnel, category, new arrivals, regional target) justifies the extra fragmentation.
cards.use_when: Adding campaigns as a store's paid social budget grows from the sub-$50k range to roughly $50k–$250k per month.

cards.title: Manage creative capacity with legitimate brand and partnership structures
cards.summary: Review active-ad capacity and genuine account needs without disguising the advertiser or evading restrictions.
cards.use_when: Running high creative volume for a large store and hitting the platform's cap on active ads on a page.

cards.title: Segment the account by region only when there is a commercial reason
cards.summary: Region segmentation should follow inventory location, fulfilment source and revenue targets, not just geography.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to split campaigns by country or consolidate regions for a store selling internationally.

cards.title: Use adset-level category segmentation instead of doubling campaigns
cards.summary: When you need category control but not full campaign duplication, hold categories at the adset level and keep one cold campaign per region.
cards.use_when: Restructuring a multi-category store's account where the brand needs category-level budget control but campaign count is already high.
